RELAY INSTRUMENT DEFECTS (opened 2026-08-05, both PROPOSE-ONLY, nothing built): (1) newest_request() is sorted(glob('*.json'))[-1] - LEXICOGRAPHIC, not mtime - and run() overwrites out_dir/<request name> with no existence check. On 2026-08-05 this re-ran a finished batch, OVERWROTE the reduction Part 2 cites by run id and sha256 (preserved at commit 946b8b7), and left the authorised batch unfetched until renamed with a last-sorting prefix. The six prior batches ran correctly by coincidence of vocabulary (1-in-36), so the mechanism had never been tested. Proposed fix ~8 lines: process every request lacking a matching result, AND refuse to overwrite an existing result - provably a no-op against the current archive. mtime-based selection is REJECTED in the record: actions/checkout destroys mtimes. (2) UNDERNEATH IT: twelve re-fetches of investmentpolicy.unctad.org returned TWELVE DISTINCT sha256 against a within-project negative control of every other host byte-identical across up to five runs. ESTABLISHED: an UNCTAD IIA sha256 is not a re-verifiable fingerprint and differing UNCTAD hashes are not evidence the page changed. NOT ESTABLISHED: the mechanism - symptom measured, cause not. CLIENT COMPLIANCE DEFECTS (opened 2026-08-09; both PROPOSE-ONLY, nothing built; both make a sentence in the PUBLISHED METHODOLOGY Part III false as written; both found with zero network, from our own source). (1) INTERVAL BYPASS: robots_allowed fetches robots.txt with requests.get DIRECTLY (src/sources/base.py:157), outside _respect_rate_limit, and polite_get calls it BEFORE _respect_rate_limit(domain) (:249 then :255). On the first fetch to any domain in a process _last_request_at has no entry, so wait is 0 and the page request follows the robots request immediately — TWO REQUESTS TO THE SAME HOST BACK TO BACK WITH NO ENFORCED INTERVAL, on every domain, every run. The 2026-08-09 batch did it four times (example.com, investmentpolicy.unctad.org, uncitral.un.org, digitallibrary.un.org — the control row is a domain like any other). METHODOLOGY Part III publishes 'I do not send automated queries to any single domain at intervals shorter than three seconds.' Fix is about two lines and is NOT applied: src/ is unapproved. (2) WILDCARD NON-SUPPORT: Python's RobotFileParser implements NO * or $ path wildcards — RuleLine.applies_to is `self.path == "*" or filename.startswith(self.path)` — so this project's robots layer SILENTLY IGNORES EVERY Disallow rule using a wildcard, on every host, and always has, while METHODOLOGY Part III publishes 'I follow standard robot exclusion protocols.' Found by the integrity officer restoring the missing colon to digitallibrary.un.org's malformed 'Disallow /record/*/export/*$' line and finding can_fetch still returned True. (3) NOT A DEFECT, A POLICY QUESTION FOR THE OPERATOR: digitallibrary.un.org publishes 'Crawl-Delay: 5'; MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS is 3.0 and grep for crawl_delay across *.py returns nothing, so the value is exposed by the parser and read by no code path. Crawl-Delay is a non-standard extension absent from RFC 9309, so this is a gap against a host's expressed preference rather than against the exclusion standard. The 2026-08-01 record already drafted the wording — 'or shorter than a longer minimum where the source publishes one' — for GDELT, a source never adopted. GAP-UNRESOLVED: rfc-9309-grammar-unverified — the disallow-line grammar and the ignore-malformed-lines rule are asserted from memory; no accessible copy of RFC 9309 was retrieved this session and none is in the repository.
